To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemotherapy‐induced sensory neuropathy (CISN) and chemotherapy‐induced motor neuropathy (CIMN) were associated with fatigue in colorectal cancer survivors.
CIPN is common in patients with colorectal cancer and that CIPN, anxiety and depression are related to each other and to fatigue.
anxiety and depression partially mediate the association of CIPN and CRC‐related fatigue, and that CIPN is a risk factor for anxiety and depression among CRC survivors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Does CIPN increase the risk of psychological distress and fatigue among CRC survivors?
the following questions: What is the prevalence of CIPN among CRC patients?
the relationship between chemotherapy‐induce peripheral neuropathy (ie, CIPN), psychological distress, and fatigue among survivors of colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between CINP and fatigue in CRC survivors can be explained by psychological stress.
CIPN is significantly associated with fatigue and that this relationship can be (partly) explained by anxiety and depression.
CIPN is a risk factor for both psychological distress and fatigue and psychological distress mediates the relationship between CINP and fatigue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anxiety and depression partially explain the association between chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy and patient-reported fatigue.
CIPN was significantly associated with both anxiety and depression and that the association between CIPN, anxiety and depression was mediated by fatigue.
CIPN is related to psychological distress (anxiety and depression) and to fatigue, and that the relationship between Cipn and fatigue can (to a certain degree) be explained by anxiety and depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CIPN is a common problem among CRC survivors, with 1 in 5 reporting moderate-to-severe symptoms.
CIPN is not only associated with fatigue, but also with psychological distress (ie anxiety and depression).
CIPN is a common and debilitating side effect of chemotherapy that can have significant negative effects on the quality of life of cancer survivors.
